subject: Requesting temporary SLO allowance for Delta preview ramp
messages:
From: Amelia Barnes <amelia@novumhealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Delta preview -- onboarding SLO question and numbers

Hi Grace / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency on the assistant flows was impressive. We are planning a soft public preview for Delta next month and I wanted to check expectations around SLOs during the preview ramp. The product team expects a bursty ramp that could reach ~450k requests/day over 2–3 weeks with peak QPS spikes during morning syncs.

Two quick asks:
- Can Redwood provisionally relax the 99th percentile latency SLO for the preview window? We can accept a higher tail if it lets us avoid blocking the launch.
- What does this provisional change mean for pricing/credits or any SLA credits? Also need to confirm uptime guarantees during the preview (we have internal launch checklists that require an SLO threshold).

I attached our rough usage estimates and a one-pager on traffic patterns (Delta-usage-estimates.xlsx). Happy to jump on a call this week if helpful.

Best,
Amelia Barnes
Product Manager, Novum Health
amelia@novumhealth.com

P.S. Procurement (procurement@novumhealth.com) has been looped for any contract tweaks.

From: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Barnes <amelia@novumhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta preview -- onboarding SLO question and numbers

Amelia — thanks for the details and the attachment. This is the right time to surface a provisional plan.

High-level proposal (internal guardrails to allow the preview):
- Temporary latency band: allow 99th percentile latency up to 750ms for the preview period (standard GA target remains 300ms).
- Uptime: maintain our standard availability commitment for control plane; for the model-serving plane we can set a provisional SLO of 99.0% for the preview window with a rollback trigger if error rates exceed thresholds.
- Duration: limited to a 28-day window from the first live traffic day for the preview.
- Operational requirements:
  - Must run a 48-hour canary at target traffic patterns with tracing enabled.
  - Enable prefix/KV caching and the suggested batching profile.
  - We will provide an explicit fallback model (compact variant) that can be routed automatically on sustained degradation.

Next steps: I will coordinate a short technical canary kickoff (infra + your engineering lead). Ben, can you sketch a draft SLO amendment and proposed fallback routing config? I will also share the internal canary checklist link.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: internal_canary_checklist.pdf (link provided in email body)

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, Amelia Barnes <amelia@novumhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 08:19:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta preview -- onboarding SLO question and numbers

Looping in infra and legal POVs (cc: Karthik). I'm supportive of Grace's proposal with two modest adjustments to reduce operational risk:

1) Add a burst capacity clause: allow short-duration burst scaling beyond reserved capacity for the 28-day window, capped at 2x steady-state QPS for no more than 10 minutes per hour. This reduces risk of cascade failures during morning spikes.
2) Slightly lower provisional uptime to 98.5% for the model-serving plane for the preview period; keeps control plane SLA at standard levels.

I've drafted an SLO amendment that captures the changes and includes rollback/notification triggers. See attached: delta_preview_slo_amendment_v1.docx. Legal will want to confirm the credit calculation; we propose a prorated credit schedule rather than full SLA credit for preview allowance.

If Novum signs off, infra will prepare the canary config and a traffic-shaping plan. Grace — please confirm if the 28-day window and the 2x/10-minute burst cap are acceptable and I will circulate to Legal for a quick tick.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Attachment: delta_preview_slo_amendment_v1.docx

From: Amelia Barnes <amelia@novumhealth.com>

Thanks — this reads sensible and pragmatic. Novum is willing to accept the provisional latency and the 28-day window. A couple of small asks from procurement/engineering:

- We need audit logs for request-level traces retained for 90 days for the preview so our compliance team can run quick audits.
- Please include the DocuSign routing for the SLO amendment and an explicit list of rollback triggers (we'll sign once legal confirms the credit schedule).
